assessment.title: Homework #7 · Transistor small-signal models
assessment.topic: Module 7 · Small-signal models · g_m, r_o · T and hybrid-π equivalents
assessment.instructions: Show the DC bias first, then the small-signal model you use (draw it in the circuit workspace), and then the gain. Short DC supplies to AC ground and coupling capacitors to short circuits. Use V_T = 25 mV. Written derivations are graded by hand; numerical checks are graded automatically. Practical task: predict first, build the schematic and breadboard yourself, check connections, test, and explain. Use Save progress in the homework toolbar, then reopen the downloaded JSON with Open saved homework. There is no homework file byte-size cap; available device memory and browser storage still apply. Keep a downloaded backup.

questions.title: 1) Common-source amplifier: bias, g_m, gain, and r_o
questions.promptHtml:
NMOS common-source amplifier: Vt = 0.4 V, kn = 4 mA/V2 (kn = kn′W/L), VGS = 0.65 V, VDD = 1.8 V, RD = 8 kΩ. Assume saturation unless found otherwise.

  1. Find the DC drain current ID and drain voltage VD.
  2. Find gm at the bias point.
  3. Find Av = vo/vgs, neglecting channel-length modulation.
  4. With λ = 0.1 V−1, find ro at the bias point and recalculate the gain.
hints: I_D = ½k_n V_OV²; check V_DS ≥ V_OV.

questions.title: 2) NMOS with R_S: source and drain gains from the T model
questions.promptHtml:
The drain connects to +VDD through RD, the source to −VSS through RS, and vi drives the gate directly. The MOSFET is in saturation with λ = 0 (ro → ∞). Replace the transistor with its small-signal T equivalent and derive:

  1. the source voltage gain vs/vi
  2. the drain voltage gain vd/vi

Numerical check: evaluate both for gm = 2 mA/V, RS = 1 kΩ, RD = 5 kΩ.
hints: In the T model the gate draws no current; a resistance 1/g_m sits between the gate and the source.
The same current i flows through 1/g_m, R_S, and out of the drain.
checklist: Draw the T model with V_DD and V_SS at AC ground.

questions.title: 3) Grounded-base BJT: V_C, g_m, and hybrid-π model
questions.promptHtml:
The transistor has a very large β, so base current may be neglected. The collector connects to +5 V through RC = 8.2 kΩ, the base is grounded, and a current source I = 0.5 mA pulls the emitter current. The input signal is coupled to the emitter through a very large capacitor (a short for small signals). Use VT = 25 mV.

  1. Find the dc collector voltage VC.
  2. Find gm.
  3. Draw the simplified hybrid-π small-signal equivalent of the transistor (use the workspace), and use it to find vc/vi.
hints: In the hybrid-π model r_π = β/g_m → ∞; the base is grounded, so v_π = 0 − v_i.
checklist: Find I_C and V_C; check the CBJ.
Draw the model: B to ground, E to v_i, g_m v_π from C to E, R_C at the collector.

questions.title: 4) Common-emitter gain with source resistance (hybrid-π)
questions.promptHtml:
A common-emitter amplifier is driven by vsig with source resistance Rsig; the bias network is not shown. Replace the transistor with its hybrid-π model (ro neglected) and determine:

  1. the input resistance Rin = vπ/ib
  2. the input voltage transmission vπ/vsig
  3. the gain vo/vπ

Then show that vo/vsig = −βRC/(rπ + Rsig).

Numerical check: β = 100, IC = 1 mA (VT = 25 mV), Rsig = 2.5 kΩ, RC = 5 kΩ.
hints: Looking into the base of the hybrid-π model you see only r_π.
β = g_m r_π links the two forms of the overall gain.
checklist: R_in, then the voltage divider R_sig–r_π.
Multiply and substitute g_m r_π = β.

questions.title: 9) Circuit Studio · From DC bias to small-signal model to measured gain (common source)
questions.promptHtml:
Start by connecting the components. The canvas contains the required components with their values, but no wires. Open Edit circuit, keep these components, and add the connections for the circuit described below. Check device pin names, source polarity and ground. Complete the schematic before using the solver or lenses. Test it on the canvas, then assemble the same circuit on the breadboard, check its wiring and compare measurements. Capture both your completed schematic and breadboard.

Circuit Studio problem · DC → AC small-signal lens, Load line, Simulate oscilloscope and Bode plot. Simulation tools are switched on for this question. Record each prediction before you use the tool that checks it.

A common-source amplifier: VDD = 12 V; gate held at VG = 2.5 V through RG = 1 MΩ; RD = 4.7 kΩ; RS = 1 kΩ bypassed by Cb; vsig with Rsig = 1 kΩ through Cin; RL = 10 kΩ through Cout. MOSFET: Vt = 1 V, kn = 2 mA/V², λ = 0.02 V⁻¹.

  1. Open Visual Aids ▾ → Load line & Q-point, click M1, and record the Q-point (VDS, ID).
  2. Predict by hand from that bias: gm = 2ID/VOV; ro = 1/(λID′) with ID′ = ½knVOV²; and Av = −gm(RD ∥ RL ∥ ro).
  3. Open Visual Aids ▾ → DC → AC small signal and step through the conversion with Next. Record ro as the lens reports it.
  4. Open Simulate, choose Oscilloscope and Run (10 mV peak, 1 kHz). Record the gain CH2/CH1. Then choose Bode plot, Run, and record the −3 dB (low) frequency.
  5. Explain: which assumptions turn the circuit into the small-signal model, and why the measured gain is unchanged in midband but falls below the −3 dB frequency.

Required build and test · Circuit Studio V2

Build the supplied common-source amplifier on schematic and breadboard, including coupling capacitors and source bypass capacitor. Check DC bias before applying a signal. Set the input to 10 mV peak at 1 kHz; connect CH1 to the gate-side input after the coupling capacitor and CH2 to the loaded output. Measure magnitude and phase of Av=vo/vi. Separately report Gv=vo/vsig if probing the generator before Rsig. Remove the source bypass capacitor, predict the gain change, test, and explain it.

  1. Record a prediction before running the solver. Match the stated component and model parameters; document any difference between the hand model and simulator.
  2. Use Edit circuit, then Build breadboard. Keep the supplied components on the canvas and connect them yourself. On the breadboard, place components and jumpers yourself; Guide me and X-Ray are allowed. Record any assistance used. Do not use Build for me as evidence of an independent build.
  3. Run the wiring check before power-on. Record the checker result, instrument terminals, source settings, measurements and units.
  4. Capture schematic, breadboard and test evidence with Capture lab evidence. For time traces, allow settling and state the measurement interval.
  5. Save progress, switch to another question and back, then reopen the downloaded progress file. Confirm that your answers, circuit, breadboard and instrument settings return.

The breadboard and measurements are virtual. Use simulated supplies only for this assignment.
hints: V_OV = V_GS − V_t with V_GS = V_G − I_D·R_S.
The low −3 dB frequency is set mainly by the bypass capacitor C_b.
